Hi everyone, I just wanted to have a bit more of a discussion on why the majority seems to hate the idea of currency as it doesn't really make sense to me.

Before we go further I would like to iterate: I read Dirtyducky's post and the thread about his perspective on the economy.

The economy, and more specifically the chestshop system, allow players to interact in a more complex manner than might be readily apparent. Ducky seemed very concerned about the value of the dollar not staying relevant as people can buy and sell nearly senseless things like dirt and cobble. This problem has an answer already built into it. If I build a chestshop with a sell feature it draws on my personal money. Therefore if you sell me cobblestone you can only sell it to me until I run out of money. I have to be careful not to set the sell price of cobble too high or I will bankrupt myself and have a chest full of cobble.

Under a pure bartering system, I have to trust that the person who has what I want/need will give it to me. For new players this can be terrifying. There are already power players who have amassed a significant amount of material wealth, what's to stop them from just taking what I have and not trading fairly? With chestshop this is impossible. These two players still interact, my name is still on the sign, but now I can't screw you out of something. If my shop is out of stock it is as simple as asking me if I have any more of an item. This also keeps the economy in check as the limited supply of items is still limited. No new blocks are generated by the chestshop. Any items that are in high demand will be priced accordingly and will be stocked accordingly. If you saw cobble for $1000 you wouldn't buy it. That seller knows when people tell him his price is too high to lower the price.

The economy is also backed by the server shop which sets a standard for pricing. If I think I can sell diamonds cheaper than 10k a stack I will and people will buy them from me instead of the server. This allows me to make equivalent money to the value of my work. Branching that idea, if A_Cure_For_Death thinks he can sell them cheaper than me he is welcome to and I will have to adjust my prices accordingly, or lose customers.

This is just a starter. I would love to hear more discussion.
Why all the hate on currency?

I like it mainly for the ability of asynchronous trading. Both parties don't have to be online for the trade to take place, all that needs to be known is the location of the shop. Further, the money can't be destroyed like items can, or be raided.

Yes, it is impersonal, but an ethereal trading system is essential on a public server.
Not only that, but since /warp lists warps someone can see my shop (once i get a warp) and go there to see what I have for sale and how that compares to other shops
Exactly. For example, I have the biggest fish shop on the server (/warp pier) and I'm a lot of peoples' source of pufferfish. I really need more people to sell puffers to me.
I had no idea there was even a fish shop, now I do though, and next time I need a puffer you'll be the first place I go, I certainly don't have time like that to wait to fish one up
Well, see, I'm almost always out of stock with puffers, so I made it so newbs can sell puffers to me. I am out of stock right now.

I do like the in-game economy, and most people can see me (No_Town) in chat either trading readily or giving away freely.

I would like to point out - however - that you state "No new blocks are generated by the chestshop." This is false as there is the /warp shop that allows a player with $5000 in game currency the ability to purchase 32 diamonds, thus bringing those diamonds into the game.

However, this is a good thing. As diamonds are rare and there is most likely a finite supply (albeit large) on server waiting to be mined, once that is all gone there will be no more diamonds left. Use up a pick here, a set of armour there, and the diamonds run dry or people with a large cache start charging ridiculous prices (1 diamond for 64 blocks of iron, etc).

With the creation of these new items into the game, it helps to curb over inflation. Charging 100$ for a diamond gives the seller slightly more then the warp shop offers, but the player charges slightly less than the warp shop cost. This also allows people the ability to purchase just a few diamonds.

Additionally, diamonds are the currency of bartering. Let's say I want 2 stacks of 64 lapis; one person could ask for 4 diamonds, another could ask for 2, and yet another just wants 1. Because I can't get lapis from the /warp shop, I either have to hunt around and find a chestshop selling lapis or I have to trade a few diamonds to get what I want.
Essentially the Adminshop backs the currency in the case that it starts to devalue!
